lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: deriving the area formula using an auxiliary altitude
lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: deriving the area formula using an auxiliary altitude

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt: In a triangle, angle A = 57°, angle B = 34°, and side a = 10 (opposite A). Find side b to two decimal places.
A triangle has sides a = 4 and b = 2 enclosing an angle of 30°. Find its area exactly.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A triangle problem gives two angles and any side (AAS or ASA). Which law should be used first?
choices: the law of sines, with a check for the ambiguous case

items.prompt: In a triangle, sides a = 12 and b = 11 enclose an angle C = 120°. Find c², the square of the third side.
In a triangle, angle A = 35°, angle B = 35°, and side a = 25 (opposite A). Find side b to two decimal places.
A triangle has sides a = 8 and b = 9 enclosing an angle of 90°. Find its area exactly.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: A triangle problem gives two sides and an angle not between them (SSA). Which law should be used first?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: In a triangle, sides a = 3 and b = 13 enclose an angle C = 60°. Find c², the square of the third side.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
